nodes.summary: MAXIMUM COVERAGE is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a maximum-coverage instance $(n, S, K, M)$ that is well formed and feasible: every subset in the list $S$ has no repeated elements and only elements less than $n$, and some sublist of $S$ with at most $K$ entries covers at least $M$ distinct elements less than $n$. nodes.title: The MAXIMUM COVERAGE decision problem

nodes.summary: A maximum-coverage instance $(n, S, K, M)$, with universe size $n$, list of subsets $S$, set budget $K$ and coverage target $M$, is feasible when there are a sublist $T$ of $S$ with at most $K$ entries and a list of at least $M$ pairwise distinct natural numbers, each less than $n$ and each belonging to some subset in $T$.
nodes.title: Feasible maximum-coverage instances

nodes.summary: A maximum-coverage instance is a tuple $(n, S, K, M)$ of a natural number $n$ (the universe size), a list $S$ of lists of natural numbers (the subsets), a natural number $K$ (the set budget) and a natural number $M$ (the coverage target).
nodes.title: Maximum-coverage instances

nodes.summary: The MAXIMUM COVERAGE decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: MAXIMUM COVERAGE is NP-complete

nodes.summary: A maximum-coverage instance $(n, S, K, M)$ is well formed when every subset in the list $S$ has no repeated elements and all of its elements are less than $n$.
nodes.title: Well-formed maximum-coverage instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
